expected_traits: 8월 다낭 평년 날씨(기온, 습도 또는 강수)
더위를 피할 수 있는 시간대 권장

results.answer:
미케비치 근처에서 8월 아침 러닝을 위한 코스, 날씨, 현지 러닝 크루 정보를 찾았어요.

## 8월 날씨 (평년값)
- **평균 최고 기온**: 35.3°C
- **평균 최저 기온**: 27.1°C
- **평균 습도**: 69%
- **월 강수량**: 132.3mm (평균 16.7일 비)
- **출처**: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (2024~2026년 8월 관측 평균)

8월은 다낭에서 가장 더운 시기 중 하나입니다. 최고 기온이 35°C를 넘고 습도도 높아 낮 시간대는 러닝하기 매우 힘듭니다. 아침 시간대(오전 5~6시 30분)는 기온이 27°C 전후로 상대적으로 낮고, 해가 뜨기 전이라 직사광선을 피할 수 있습니다. 현지 러너들과 가이드 모두 이른 아침 러닝을 권장하며, 정오는 커피나 식사 시간으로 남겨두라고 조언합니다.

물을 충분히 챙기고, 더위에 익숙하지 않다면 페이스를 천천히 시작하세요. 뛸지 여부는 본인의 컨디션과 더위 적응 정도에 따라 판단하시면 됩니다.

---

## 미케비치 근처 러닝 코스

| 코스 이름 | 거리 | 고저차 | 숙소에서 거리 | 특징 | 출처 |
|---------|------|--------|-------------|------|------|
| **미케비치 해변 + 산책로** | 최대 30km (산책로 구간 6km) | 0m (평탄) | 0km (해변가) | 넓고 평탄한 백사장, 물가 쪽 모래가 단단해 러닝 가능. My An에서 북쪽으로 6km 구간은 해변 산책로(promenade)가 있어 야자수 그늘과 바다 전망 제공. 일출 러닝 명소 | [Great Runs](https://greatruns.com/da-nang-my-khe-beach/), [Visit Vietnam](https://www.visitvietnam.net/blog/da-nang-running-routes/) |
| **Công viên Hồ Nghinh** | 0.47km (공원 둘레) | 0m | 0.43km | 작은 공원 둘레 코스, 여러 바퀴 가능 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/962130353) |
| **My Khe Beach Park** | 0.88km (공원 둘레) | 2m | 2.59km | 공원 둘레 코스 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/780440810) |
| **육상 트랙** | 0.43km (1바퀴) | 4m | 2.5km | 표준 육상 트랙 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1254925475) |
| **한강 산책로 + 다리 루프** | 5~10km | 확인 불가 | 약 3~4km | 평탄한 강변 산책로, Dragon Bridge, Tran Thi Ly Bridge 등을 건너 루프 코스 가능. 아침과 저녁 모두 인기 | [Visit Vietnam](https://www.visitvietnam.net/blog/da-nang-running-routes/) |
| **선짜반도 (Son Tra Peninsula)** | 유연 조정 가능 | 확인 불가 (언덕 코스) | 약 5km | Hoang Sa Street에서 Linh Ung Pagoda까지 오르막 코스. 숲과 바다 전망, 긴 오르막과 헤어핀 커브. 경험 있는 러너 추천 | [Visit Vietnam](https://www.visitvietnam.net/blog/da-nang-running-routes/) |

**추천 코스**: 미케비치 해변 산책로는 숙소에서 바로 출발 가능하고, 평탄하며, 일출 시간대(오전 5~6시 30분)에 가장 아름답습니다. 5km는 왕복 2.5km 지점에서 돌아오고, 10km는 Son Tra 방향이나 Truong Sa 방향으로 더 달리면 됩니다.

The My Khe Beach area is the signature place to run in Da Nang. This wide, flat beach opens out to the East Vietnam Sea, and stretches for some 30 km. The sand is soft, but generally firm enough for running, especially near the water. There is also a 
beachside promenade path
, paralleling the main road, from My An heading north for ~6 km.  Enjoy white sand, sea views, and some shaded sections with coconut trees. 
Our thanks to Pekka Myllyla (
runaroundasia.com
) for his insights on this route!
Pekka Myllyla
One can start anywhere along the beach (probably depending on what hotel you’re staying at!), but a good place to start is in My An. From here, the beach heads north for about 6 km, and this is also the section where the promenade path goes as well. From My An heading south toward Hoi An, it’s mainly a beach run, with hotels and golf courses dotting the main road, which turns inland. There are bus stops at certain points, so it is possible to do a one-way run and expose your sweaty self for the return 🙂
Longer Run
: At the northern end of the beach, Hoàng Sa road turns right toward Danang Green Lake and the Vườn Lộc Uyển Buddhist Temple. The hilly main road has a decent shoulder for running.

Run the City Awake: Da Nang's Best 5 - 10 km Routes for Runners
07/06/2026
Three scenic 5–10K running routes in Da Nang, from the Han River and My Khe Beach to Son Tra Peninsula, best enjoyed before the city fully wakes up.
The best way to get to know Da Nang is to run through it before the sun gets too high
Some cities are best introduced through a taxi window. Da Nang, though, makes more sense in running shoes, especially before six in the morning, when the air is still cool, the riverside and beachfront belong to early risers, and the sea is just beginning to turn pink.
This city feels made for running. The riverfront is long and flat. The coastal road is wide, open, and breezy. The bridges sit close enough together to turn into easy loops. And when you want something that asks a little more from your legs, Son Tra Peninsula is right there, green, steep, and just difficult enough to keep you humble.
Here are three routes that are scenic without being complicated, all within a runner-friendly 5-10km range. You can take them slow and use them to see the city, or hold a steadier pace if you are training for a race. Lace up; the best one is saved for last, and it comes with a sunrise.
The riverside loop: Han River promenade and city bridges
If you want an easy first run in Da Nang, start by the Han River. This is a gentle city route in the best way: flat paths, wide pavements, morning walkers, local runners, and the river quietly reflecting the bridges beside you.
On the west bank, the stretch around Bach Dang Street toward Thuan Phuoc Bridge is an easy place to begin. You can run out and back for a neat 5K. If you want something more interesting, turn it into a loop: cross one bridge, run along the opposite bank, then return by another. Han River Bridge, Dragon Bridge, Tran Thi Ly Bridge, and Thuan Phuoc Bridge can all become part of the route, depending on how far you want to go.
Morning is the most comfortable time, before the sun gets too strong and the city is still warming up slowly. Evening has its own charm too, with bridge lights on the water, cooler air, and a livelier atmosphere. Just keep in mind that the Dragon Bridge area gets crowded on weekends, especially around the fire and water show. It is beautiful, but not ideal if you care about pace.
Anchor points: Dragon Bridge, Bach Dang Street, the Han River banks, or East Sea Park if you want to connect to the beachfront.
Distance: 5K out and back; 7–10K if you loop across the bridges.
Best time: 5:00–6:30 AM or after sunset.
The hill climb: Son Tra Peninsula
When you want to trade flat pavement for a little punishment, head toward Son Tra. From the base of the peninsula on Hoang Sa Street, the road starts climbing into the green. Long inclines, hairpin bends, and sudden sea views around the corners make this route beautiful, but it also deserves respect.
This is not the route for a casual midday jog. Son Tra is better for runners who already have some mileage in their legs, especially those training for hills, endurance, a half marathon, a full marathon, or a trail race. You can adjust the difficulty as you go. Running up to Linh Ung Pagoda and turning back is already a solid morning effort. If your legs are good, the weather is kind, and the road conditions allow, you can push farther toward Ban Co Peak.
The memorable part of Son Tra is not only the climb. It is the way the city disappears behind you so quickly, replaced by forest, wind, and flashes of blue sea through the trees. If you are lucky, you may even spot a red-shanked douc high in the canopy. Running here feels less like moving through a city and more like stepping into a very different side of Da Nang.
Start early, ideally around first light. Bring your own water, because there are almost no convenient places to refill along the route. Wear something visible if you begin before sunrise, and stay alert, as parts of the road are narrow and shared with motorbikes and cars.
Anchor points: Hoang Sa Street → Linh Ung Pagoda → optional extension toward Ban Co Peak.
Distance: Flexible depending on your turnaround point; hilly and better for stronger runners.
Best time: Sunrise; avoid midday.
🛵
Curious about Son Tra without running it? Try exploring the peninsula by motorbike instead, when you can slow down, stop longer, and save your legs for the views.
The sunrise route: My Khe Beach
This is the route worth setting an early alarm for. The coastal road, Vo Nguyen Giap connecting into Hoang Sa, follows the long golden stretch of My Khe Beach and gives you one of the easiest, breeziest runs in Da Nang: flat, open, wide, sea-cooled, and full of that quiet feeling of a city waking up beside you.
Start around East Sea Park and follow the beachfront path. For a 5K, pick a point about 2.5 km away and turn back. For a 10K, keep your rhythm a little longer toward Son Tra or down toward Truong Sa. This is the kind of route where the kilometers can pass almost without you noticing, because there is always something to look at: locals exercising, rows of palms, the sea, small boats in the distance, and then the sun slowly lifting out of the water.
The best window is around 5:00–6:30 AM. A little before sunrise, the sky is still blue-grey and quiet. Then the sea begins to shift into orange and pink before the day fully brightens. You may not run your fastest here, because at some point you will probably want to slow down and look. That is also the reason this route is so worth doing.
Quietly, this may be one of the most beautiful urban running routes in Vietnam. It is also one of the simplest ways to fall for Da Nang.
Anchor points: East Sea Park, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Hoang Sa Street, My Khe Beach.
Distance: 5–10K, flat and suitable for many levels.
Best time: 5:00–6:30 AM for sunrise.
Running tips in Da Nang
Avoid the heat. Da Nang is warm and humid for much of the year, so sunrise and after sunset are the most comfortable windows. Midday is better saved for coffee or a proper meal, not for forcing out a few kilometers under the sun.
Carry water. Along the beach and river, you can usually find cafés or shops after your run, but not every stretch has easy water access while you are moving. On Son Tra, you should be even more prepared.
You will not be running alone. Early mornings in Da Nang are full of people walking, jogging, stretching, and exercising by the river and beach. That friendly local rhythm makes solo running feel easier and safer.
Watch the traffic. Use promenades and walking paths whenever possible. On Son Tra, the roads are narrower and shared with motorbikes and cars, so stay to the side, wear visible clothing, and keep your attention on the road.
If you are new to running, start flat. The Han River and My Khe Beach routes are smooth, wide, and forgiving. Save Son Tra for a day when you actually want to climb.
If you are chasing a race, Da Nang hosts international marathon events during the year. Check the current race calendar if you want to plan your trip around one.
And finally, reward yourself. Finishing a run near the river or the sea means you are only a few steps from good coffee, mi Quang, banh mi, or a proper Vietnamese breakfast. In Da Nang, the post-run meal is very much part of the route.

 – Tag. In Motion
      How to Find a Running Club in Da Nang: What to Expect on Your First Run
Joining a 
running club
 for the first time can feel a little intimidating. You don’t know anyone, you’re not sure what pace everyone runs, and there’s always that thought in the back of your mind that you might turn up and immediately realise everyone is much faster than you.
Thankfully, that feeling normally lasts about five minutes.
Once the run starts, things become pretty simple. You find a pace that feels comfortable, start talking to whoever happens to be running next to you and, before long, you’re back at the meeting point wondering why you spent so much time thinking about it in the first place.
If you’re new to Da Nang, or you’ve been 
running in Da Nang
 alone for a while, joining a local 
running club
 is also a great way to get to know the city and meet people outside your usual circle.
Here’s what you can expect when you come along for the first time.
You don’t need to be a fast runner
Probably worth getting this one out of the way first.
There are some seriously good runners in Da Nang. There are also plenty of people who run simply because they enjoy it, people working towards their first 10K, and people who have absolutely no interest in chasing a PB every weekend.
A good 
running community
 has room for all of them.
Group runs tend to settle into different paces naturally, so there’s no reason your first session needs to become a test of how fast you can run. Start comfortably, get a feel for the group and go from there.
After a few weeks, you’ll probably notice something else too. Pace becomes much less important once you start knowing everyone. The run is still the reason you meet, but catching up with people becomes part of why you keep coming back.
What happens on your first run?
Honestly, it’s pretty straightforward.
Try to arrive a little before the start time. It gives you a chance to say hello, find out what the session looks like and meet a few people before everyone heads off. Depending on the day, there might be a set route or a more structured training session.
As for what to bring, there’s no special kit list. Wear running shoes you’re comfortable in, something suitable to run in and bring water if you need it. Da Nang gets hot and humid enough without carrying half a running shop around with you.
You definitely don’t need a carbon-plated shoe, GPS watch and hydration vest for your first 5K with the group. Although, to be fair, give it a few months and you might somehow end up owning all three.
That tends to happen.
Different days, different runs
One of the things we like about running together is that every session doesn’t need to serve the same purpose.
A relaxed run around the city gives you some easy kilometres and time to chat. Interval sessions are there when you want to push things a little harder, while longer weekend runs are useful when you’re building towards a race or simply feel like spending more time on your feet.
At 
TAG Running Club
, we run three times during the week and mix those sessions up. You don’t need to attend every one of them, and plenty of people don’t.
Come to the sessions that suit you. If you’re training for something, use the group as part of that training. If you just want a reason to get out and run after work, that works too.
Running around Da Nang
We’re pretty lucky with where we get to run.
The coastline is the obvious choice, particularly early in the morning before the city gets busy. Then there’s the Han River, the bridges and plenty of streets that feel completely different when you’re moving through them on foot rather than sitting on a motorbike.
Of course, summer adds another dimension. There’s nothing quite like stepping outside for an “easy run” and realising Da Nang has other plans for you.
Running in Da Nang
 with a local group also helps you learn the city surprisingly quickly. You pick up new routes, work out where people like to run at different times of day and, equally important, discover where everyone goes for coffee afterwards.
For people who have recently moved to Da Nang, that social side can be just as valuable as the running itself. Meeting people in a new city isn’t always easy. Turning up somewhere where you already know everyone shares at least one interest makes it a lot simpler.
So, how do you choose a running club?
There isn’t really a complicated answer to this.
Look at when they run and what sort of sessions they organise, but don’t spend too much time trying to compare every 
running club in Da Nang
 from your phone. A club can have the perfect schedule and still not be your kind of place.
Go for a run with them instead.
You’ll get a pretty good feeling for the community after one or two sessions. If you enjoy the run and like the people, come back. That matters much more than finding the supposedly “best” club in the city.
Running with TAG
TAG started with running, but the community has grown into something bigger than simply meeting up to collect kilometres.
We train together, enter races, hang out and occasionally convince each other that waking up ridiculously early on a Saturday is a perfectly normal thing to do. There are people who take their training seriously and people who are mostly there for the social side. Most of us are probably a mixture of both.
If you’ve been looking for a 
running club in Da Nang
, you’re welcome to come along and see what it’s like.
There’s no need to wait until you’re fitter or faster. You don’t need to know anyone beforehand either. Check the next session, turn up and introduce yourself.
The first run is usually the hardest one to join.
After that, it’s just another run with people you know.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is TAG Running Club suitable for beginners?
Yes. 
TAG Running Club
 has runners with different levels of experience, so you don’t need to be particularly fast or be training for a race to join. If you’re relatively new to running, take the first few sessions at a comfortable pace and build from there.
Do I need to register before joining a TAG run?
Check TAG’s latest schedule before you come along, as the meeting point, time and type of session can vary. Arriving a little early for your first session is always a good idea too.
What should I bring?
For most runs, comfortable running shoes and normal running clothes are enough. Bring water if you need it and keep the weather in mind — Da Nang can be very hot and humid.
Where can I run in Da Nang?
The beachfront and Han River are two of the most popular areas for 
running in Da Nang
, with plenty of options for both short and longer routes. Running with a local community is also a good way to discover quieter routes around the city that you might not come across on your own.
How do I find a running club near me in Da Nang?
If you’re searching for a 
running club near me
 in Da Nang, you can find local groups through social media or search for a 
Da Nang running club
 online. Once you find one that fits your schedule, the best way to know whether it suits you is simply to join a session.
If you’d like to run with 
TAG Running Club
, check our latest schedule and come say hello.
